A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIPO study. Their main text, equations, Tables 1–7, Figures 1–5 and Appendices A–E support a complete comparison; the additional page in v6 results from reflow.

before.justification: v5 reports original MIPO experiments on personalization, mathematics and multiple-choice questions, including benchmark results, 70B-model evaluation and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v6 reports original MIPO benchmark results, 70B-model evaluation, negative-sampling ablations and supplementary empirical analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same contrastive preference construction, DPO objective, conditional personalization variant, and missing, random and reshuffled negative-sampling strategies.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Community Alignment, PRISM, Multifaceted Bench, GSM8k, SVAMP and ARC-Easy/Challenge. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain identical: prompting, SFT variants, PPO with MI, RLAIF variants, InfoNCE, SAMI and RLVR retain their participation in the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendices D–E retain the same splits, sample sizes, model configurations, training budgets, judges and metrics, including eight-shot math evaluation and the existing 70B protocol.

E4.justification: The negative-sampling and negative-count ablations, random-string controls, critic analysis, diversity and entropy analyses, learning curves and Appendix C examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same seed and uncertainty reporting, including the three-seed mean/standard-deviation practice and Qwen-7B exception stated in Appendix E. No statistical procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched values and findings in Tables 1–7, Figures 2–5 and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains the Llama-3.2-1B MIPO GSM score of 29.5 ± 2.29; the 70B comparison results also match.

T1.justification: The DPO–InfoNCE derivation, pointwise and conditional mutual-information objectives, and negative-sampling assumptions remain unchanged. Equations move across columns or pages without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about contrastive self-training without additional supervision and improvements in personalization, mathematics and multiple-choice tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning fixed-reference rewards, diversity, scaling and negative sampling are retained. The limitations concerning LLM judges, GPT-4o context extraction and weak intrinsic training signals are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E retain the prompts, preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters, hardware and code-access information. Updating the OpenRLHF citation from 2024 to 2025 does not report a software or implementation change.

R1.justification: Section 2 qualifies its characterization of prior personalization methods: reliance on human preferences becomes reliance on human or mixed real/synthetic preferences. This modestly refines research positioning; the updated bibliographic entries identify retained works.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to the Section 2 qualification, citation and bibliography updates, and version stamp. Updates include Koala’s author name, OpenRLHF’s author list/year, and Li et al.’s title/year. The narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Text reflow shifts equations and retained displays, including Tables 1 and 3 and Figures 2–3. The limitations now end on a mostly empty v6 page 10, shifting subsequent material by one page. Figure and table designs and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The related-work qualification and bibliographic updates offer small editorial refinements. The scientific argument, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, while reflow leaves a mostly empty limitations continuation page. These limited changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
